guarantees.claim: msg_mask_permuted is assigned to the permutation of static_mask according to RndCnstMsgPerm: for each bit index i from 0 to MsgWidth-1, msg_mask_permuted[i] = static_mask[RndCnstMsgPerm[i]].
When MsgWidth is 0, the loop does not execute and msg_mask_permuted remains at its default all-zero value.

assumptions.claim: For every i in 0..MsgWidth-1, RndCnstMsgPerm[i] must be a valid index into the static_mask array (i.e., within bounds of static_mask).
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds indexing can cause X-propagation, simulation mismatch, and invalid mask values.

uncertain_points.claim: The design uses a static mask (static_mask) rather than a dynamic LFSR-based mask, which may reduce DPA resistance because the same mask bits are reused every operation.
uncertain_points.cond: always (if this masking serves as a side-channel countermeasure)
uncertain_points.risk: Reduced power-analysis protection, potentially leaking secret-dependent information.

uncertain_points.claim: RndCnstMsgPerm is used as an index permutation, but it is not clear whether it is a full permutation covering all static_mask bits. Duplicate indices or missing indices would lower mask entropy.
uncertain_points.risk: Reduced mask entropy can weaken DPA countermeasure effectiveness.
